target_customer: Indian students and expats moving to the United States who need a US bank account, credit and a SIM before arrival
problem: New arrivals have no US credit history or SSN, so they cannot easily open accounts or get cards and pay high remittance fees.
business_model: Neobank style fintech: interchange, FX and remittance fees, partner revenue (inferred from product mix, not stated)

competitors.name: Nova Credit
competitors.what: Lets immigrants bring foreign credit history to US lenders
competitors.traction_then: Reaches nearly 60 percent of 2.5 million yearly US immigrants per its CEO; partners include Mpower and Yardi
competitors.funding_then: Nearly $20M per Crunchbase cited by CNBC

technical_complexity.rationale: Built on banking-as-a-service partners, a card program and an MVNO SIM resale, so mostly integration and compliance work rather than novel technology.

defensibility.rationale: Depends on partner bank and card program relationships; a niche community focus helps but competitors could offer the same bundle.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: A source search showed later entrants such as Remitly Passbook and Zolve in the same niche; no acquisition of Swadesh found.

market_need_then: Nova Credit coverage in December 2018 shows about 2.5 million immigrants arrive in the US each year and lack portable financial identity.

branding.domain_note: Uses swadesh.co and a bank-style product name; no purchase history found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Reassuring and benefit focused; leads with safety and savings

brand_strength.rationale: Hindi-language name signals the target community, but no press about the brand or community assets were found and the name may be hard for non-Hindi speakers.

pivots.from: Free US bank account, credit card, SIM and remittances for new immigrants
pivots.to: Neobank for Indian students and expats opened from India with passport and visa
pivots.why: The website now emphasizes onboarding before arrival; no dated source for the shift.

outcome_analysis: Swadesh joined YC in Summer 2019 to give Indian immigrants a US bank account, card, SIM and cheaper remittances. The only verified round found is a 2.25 million dollar pre-seed announced in July 2022 from Khosla Ventures, Y Combinator, 8VC and Section32. The company is active and now onboards customers from India, but traction figures are not public.
notes: Pre-seed amount and investors stated by Inc42 and Venture Intelligence (two outlets). Latka shows $0 funding and one profile lists about 97 employees; both unverified. The website fetch of www.swadesh.co succeeded on the second try. The meaning of the name was not found in any source and is left null. Only one competitor had a source dated before the batch.
